parole.significato: an item not designed to be used as a weapon, but used as a weapon nevertheless, such as a hammer used as a murder weapon
parole.testo: Probably from Old East Slavic [script needed] (ostén).

parole.significato: A type of traditional long underpants.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Old East Slavic *гачѣ (*gačě), from Proto-Slavic *gaťę.

parole.significato: wire fish-trap
parole.testo: Borrowed from Old East Slavic котьци (kotĭci); the origin of the -ka is not certain, but might also have a Slavic origin.

parole.significato: sliver, rolag (a roll of woolen fibre to spin yarn)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Old East Slavic *кѫдѣль (*kǫdělĭ), from Proto-Slavic *kǫdělь.

parole.significato: distaff
parole.testo: From Old East Slavic [Term?] (compare Russian кужель (kuželʹ), Czech kužel).

parole.significato: barge
parole.testo: From Old East Slavic лодья (lodĭja).

parole.significato: barn, cowhouse, cow/sheep/etc. barn
parole.testo: Borrowed from Old East Slavic хлѣвъ (xlěvŭ). Compare Russian хлев (xlev, “barn”). Cognate with Karelian liävä.

parole.significato: quite large or abundant; quite a
parole.testo: Possibly borrowed from Old East Slavic мѣлъкъ (mělŭkŭ), Russian мелкий (melkij), with + -eä. Cognate with Karelian melkie.

parole.significato: Muromian (person)
parole.testo: From Old East Slavic Мурома (Muroma).

parole.significato: amount, quantity, volume
parole.testo: Borrowed from Old East Slavic мѣра (měra) (compare Russian ме́ра (méra)), from Proto-Slavic *měra. The same word was also borrowed (likely independently) to other Finnic languages, such as Estonian määr, Ingrian määrä, Karelian miärä, Livvi miäry, Veps mär, Votic määre. Details Both SSA and NSES lis

parole.significato: parish
parole.testo: Borrowed from Old East Slavic погостъ (pogostŭ). Doublet of pokosta. Cognates include Latvian pagasts, Livonian pagāst and Russian пого́ст (pogóst).

parole.significato: pie (type of pastry that consists of an outer crust and a filling)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Old East Slavic пирогъ (pirogŭ), with the nominative constructed by analogy from the oblique stem piiraga- > piiraa- (compare saapas).

parole.significato: reed (comb-like part of a beater for beating the weft when weaving)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Old East Slavic бьрдо (bĭrdo), ultimately from Proto-Slavic *bьrdo. Finnic cognates include Estonian piird, Karelian pirta, Livvi pirdu, Ludian bird, Veps bird, Votic pirtõ.

parole.significato: cabin, cottage (especially one with heating, particularly a savupirtti)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Old East Slavic пьрть (pĭrtĭ) (compare Russian перть (pertʹ), but also Latvian pirts, Lithuanian pirtis). Akin to Karelian pirtti and Veps pertʹ.

parole.significato: shive, splinter (such as on flax or paper)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Old East Slavic [Term?] (compare Russian па́здер (pázder)). Cognate with Ingrian päissär, Karelian päissär, Ludian päštäŕ, Veps pästred, Votic päisser.

parole.significato: Bible, (a) bible (an individual copy of Raamattu, or the Bible)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Old East Slavic грамота (gramota), from Ancient Greek γράμματα (grámmata, “letters, writing”). According to Häkkinen (2018), the word was borrowed through Estonian raamat, to which it is at least definitely related. If the word is borrowed from Estonian, it likely originally simply mea

parole.significato: border, boundary, limit, line (line or frontier area separating political or geographical regions)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Old East Slavic краи (krai) (genitive краꙗ (kraja), compare Russian край (kraj)), from Proto-Slavic *krajь. The same word was also borrowed into other Finnic languages, such as Estonian raja, Ingrian raja, Karelian raja, Ludian raja, Votic raja.

parole.significato: to nourish (feed and cause to grow)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Old East Slavic [Term?] (whence Russian страви́ть (stravítʹ)) and suffixed with -ita, from Proto-Slavic *trāvìti. Related to Estonian ravima and Karelian ravittoa.

parole.significato: nuisance, annoyance, peeve
parole.testo: Probably borrowed from Old East Slavic грѣза (grěza, “dream, delirium, confusion”).

parole.significato: breed (all animals or plants of the same species or subspecies, such as of domesticated animals)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Old East Slavic родъ (rodŭ) (compare Russian ро́д (ród, “kind”)).

parole.significato: boot (shoe)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Old East Slavic сапогъ (sapogŭ), from Proto-Slavic *sapogъ. The nominative and partitive singular stem is analogical from earlier saappaa < *saappaga (compare piiras). Compare Karelian šuappua, Livvi suappai, Veps sapag, Estonian saabas.

parole.significato: shuttle (part of a loom)
parole.testo: Uncertain. One possibility considered is a loan from Old East Slavic *съкальꙗ (*sŭkalĭja) (compare Russian скалья́ (skalʹjá)). Another is relation to sukkela (“quick, swift”) (as the shuttle is sent back and forth during weaving; compare the synonym syöstävä from syöstä). Related to Ingrian sukkulai

parole.significato: battle axe, axe (weapon)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Old East Slavic топоръ (toporŭ), from Proto-Slavic *toporъ; compare Russian топо́р (topór, “axe”).

parole.significato: Chud, Chude (person)
parole.testo: From Old East Slavic чудь (čudĭ, “Chud”).

parole.significato: synonym of vesikko
parole.testo: Borrowed from Old East Slavic [Term?] (compare Proto-Slavic *dъxorь, Russian хорь (xorʹ)). Possibly later associated with tuhka by folk etymology.

parole.significato: marketplace
parole.testo: Borrowed from Old East Slavic търгъ (tŭrgŭ, “market place”) (perhaps through Estonian turg), from Proto-Slavic *tъrgъ. Cognate to Swedish torg and Estonian turg. Doublet of tori.

parole.significato: pain, distress, agony, suffering, anguish, torment
parole.testo: Borrowed from Old East Slavic тъска (tŭska) (compare Russian тоска́ (toská, “melancholy”)). Akin to Ludian tusk.

parole.significato: Chud, Chude (person)
parole.testo: From Old East Slavic чудь (čudĭ, “Chud”).

parole.significato: gate, wicket (simple, light gate, particularly one intended to keep animals on their side of it)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Old East Slavic верѣꙗ (verěja) (compare e.g. Russian верея́ (verejá)), from Proto-Slavic *verěja. Estonian värav, Karelian veräjä, Veps verai and Votic väräje have the same origin.

parole.significato: strong gust of wind, gale, squall
parole.testo: From Old East Slavic вихърь (vixŭrĭ).

parole.significato: an old Finnish unit of length, equivalent to 1068.80 m, or one-tenth of a peninkulma
parole.testo: Borrowed from Old East Slavic вьрста (vĭrsta), from Proto-Slavic *vьrsta.

parole.significato: birchbark shoe (shoe made by weaving strips of birchbark, used earlier in Scandinavia and elsewhere in the boreal fores…
parole.testo: Borrowed from Old East Slavic *вьрзъ (*vĭrzŭ).

parole.significato: spindle; distaff (rod in spinning and winding thread)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Old East Slavic веретено (vereteno), from Proto-Slavic *verteno (“spindle”). Compare Estonian värten, Livvi värtin and Veps värtin.
